text:
josh: Heads up — getting intermittent 401s when streaming from Node and Go clients. Tracked it down to an API key that had a trailing tab in the file. Anyone seen trailing-tab/tiny invisible chars break Basic auth before?
elaine: yep, seen that. Windows editors or copy-paste can sneak in tabs or non-printables. What exact header are you forming?
mika: Common pitfall: using `echo $KEY | base64` adds a newline. Use `echo -n` or `printf` so the base64 payload is exact.
josh: We're doing Basic auth with the key as username and empty password, so header is `Authorization: Basic <base64>` where base64 is of `KEY:`. Example that bit me: `export REDWOOD_KEY=$(cat keyfile)` (keyfile had a trailing tab). Then `Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' "$REDWOOD_KEY:" | base64)` produced a different value than the SDK test vector.
elaine: Could be subtle differences across shells. Quick checks: `xxd -g 1 -u -c 256 keyfile` to show invisible bytes, or `cat -v keyfile` to surface `^I`.
josh: Repro steps I used: 
```
# wrong (file contains trailing tab)
export REDWOOD_KEY="$(cat keyfile)"
curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' "$REDWOOD_KEY:" | base64)" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
This returned 401. After trimming tab it works.
mika: For robustness, normalize at startup: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(tr -d '\r\n\t' < keyfile)` or in code `strings.TrimSpace(strings.ReplaceAll(key, "\t", ""))`. Also beware `TrimSpace` removes newlines/spaces but not necessarily other control chars; explicitly strip `\t`/`\r`.
elaine: For Node: `Buffer.from(key + ':').toString('base64')` is correct but make sure `key` is trimmed. For Go: `base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(key + ":"))`. Example: `req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Basic "+b64)` — ensure key has no trailing tab.
mika: Note on streaming: if the initial handshake succeeds but a subsequent retry re-reads the env with different sanitization (or an entrypoint script modifies it), you can get a mid-stream 401. Add a one-time validation at SDK init that decodes the header and checks pattern (e.g., length / allowed chars).
josh: Good call. I'll add an SDK startup sanity check that fails fast and logs the decoded username length and nonprintables. Also adding a small helper `normalizeApiKey()` that callers can opt into.
elaine: Devex doc suggestion: add a snippet under "Auth setup" — `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(tr -d '\r\n\t' < keyfile)` and `# or: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat keyfile | xargs printf "%s")`.
mika: Kubernetes note: when creating secrets, prefer `--from-literal=REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat keyfile | tr -d '\r\n\t')` or `kubectl create secret generic redwood --from-file=keyfile --dry-run=client -o yaml | yq eval '.data.keyfile |= @base64' -` so you control whitespace.
ci-bot: ci: branch fix/trim-apikey — lint ✅, unit tests ✅, integration streaming test flaky=0/20 ✅. Build #234 succeeded.
josh: Thanks all. I'll push the SDK PR and a short devex blurb. Ping me if you want to test with your environment. :thumbsup:
